conbody.p: Using a password with 16 or more characters is more difficult to break. Thereat actors can test a lot of password combinations very quickly, so the longer the password is the more secure it is
Attackers look for predictable password patterns and common character substitutions, so ensuring that you avoid these things can make your password more secure.

Having a different password for each accoun ensures that if one password is breached, those credentials cannot be used for other accounts and systems which could lead to further compromised data and systems.

When passwords are reset frequently employees typically recycle old passwords, create weaker variations on thier current ones, write those passwords down, or make small predictable changes. These make it more vulnerable, so only changing passwords when there is evedeince or suspicon of a break prevents these occurances.
Using Multi-Factor Authentication significantly decreases the liklihood of unathorized access bec ause it requires additional information to sign in.
